{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "He did not sit. He stood by the range with the kettle starting to breathe behind him and looked at the envelope the way a man looks at a fence he has been meaning to mend.

"He'd know," Aldous said. "He'd know I'd stand here like a fool."

"He said that too."

She had taken off her gloves and laid them one across the other on her knee. Her hands were red from the cold and she did not rub them. He found himself grateful for that as well, though he could not have said why. Perhaps because it meant she was not going to ask him for anything. Perhaps because it meant she had already asked, in her way, by standing at the gate for as long as she had.

The kettle began to sing and he took it off before it could get loud. He made the tea properly this time, warming the pot, counting the spoons. When he set a cup in front of her she thanked him and did not touch it.

"Forty years," he said. "Forty-one in March."

"I know."

"He tell you why?"

"No." She nodded at the envelope. "But I'd guess that does."

Aldous sat down at last, across from her, the table between them and the letter between them and the whole of what he had not said between them. He put his thumb under the flap. The paper was old and gave at once, as if it had been waiting, as if it too had been given the time."}
